rounds.text: A B Infrabuild Ltd is demonstrating exceptional top-line and bottom-line expansion, with compounded sales growing at 33% over 5 years [E15] and profit compounding at an impressive 66% over the same period [E19]. This robust fundamental momentum is further highlighted by recent performance metrics, including a stellar net profit surge of 134% YoY and sales accelerating by 99% YoY [E63, E65]. The company generates solid returns with a 15.2% ROCE [E12] and a consistent 15% median return on equity over a 5-year span [E26]. Valuation-wise, a discounted cash flow model values the intrinsic worth at Rs 14 per share against the current market price of Rs 12.2 [E43], providing a positive margin of safety [E44] while the reverse DCF indicates that the market's current expectations are overly conservative compared to reality [E45]. Conceded: promoter holding is low at 30.94% [E39] and operating cash flow turned negative at Rs -51 Cr in March 2026 [E34].

The valuation is stretched across multiple metrics, trading at a P/E of 33.8x [E1] and a P/B of 4.34x [E2], with key-ratios showing an even higher P/E of 40.35x and EV/EBITDA of 20.05x against sector benchmarks of 13.57x and 8.29x respectively [E6, E11]. Fundamental cash generation presents severe strains, highlighted by negative operating cash flow of Rs -51 Cr and free cash flow of -63 Cr in March 2026, leading to an alarming cash conversion ratio of -2.68x [E33, E34, E35]. Working capital deterioration compounds these cash generation pressures, as debtor days have ballooned from 92.8 to 148 days [E60], while borrowings have concurrently risen to Rs 139 Cr in September 2026 from Rs 115 Cr a year prior [E37]. Insider alignment is weakening through promoter selling, with holdings dropping by 5.88 percentage points over three years to 30.94% [E39, E61], and the equity trades under clear technical distress below both its 50-day and 200-day moving averages alongside a 32.7% twelve-month price return decline [E48, E50]. Conceded: the company has delivered strong historical profit growth of 65.9% CAGR over the last 5 years and trades below its DCF value [E43, E58].

Conceded: valuation metrics show a P/E of 33.8x, P/B of 4.34x, and elevated relative ratios [E1, E2, E6, E7, E11], alongside rising borrowings to Rs 139 Cr [E37], a twelve-month price decline of 32.7% [E50], and promoter holdings decreasing by 5.88 percentage points to 30.94% [E39, E61]. However, the severe cash flow strains are heavily countered by exceptional fundamental performance, including net profit surging 134% YoY and sales growing 99% YoY, earning results a stellar score of 95/100 [E63, E65, E69]. This massive operational acceleration invalidates stale sentiment, supported by a rules-based screen scoring 74/100 [E62], positive institutional money flow [E42], and a discounted cash flow valuation placing intrinsic value above the current market price [E43]. Furthermore, the company commands a strong historical profit growth of 65.9% CAGR over the last five years [E58], proving that recent price-led disconnects [E55] overlook explosive underlying expansion.

Conceded: net profit surged 134% YoY and sales grew 99% YoY [E63, E65], earning results a score of 95/100 [E69]. However, pointing to a DCF intrinsic value of Rs 14 [E43] or a rules-based score of 74/100 [E62] ignores that these metrics are completely undermined by catastrophic cash flow destruction, with free cash flow plummeting to negative Rs 63 Cr and cash conversion hitting -2.68x [E33, E35]. The argument that explosive expansion validates the valuation [E58] crumbles against severe working capital decay, explicitly evidenced by debtor days ballooning from 92.8 to 148 days [E60]. Furthermore, citing positive institutional money flow [E42] does not erase the ongoing structural exit by insiders, with promoter holding shrinking down to 30.94% [E39]. Finally, dismissing the stock's -32.7% twelve-month return [E50] and its position below both the 50-day and 200-day moving averages [E48] as stale sentiment [E69] overlooks the historical reality of a devastating 78.3% peak-to-trough drawdown [E51] and an annualized volatility of 56.1% [E52].
